text:
My birds say Seat-04’s kettle is warm, but the pot is empty.
My birds say Seat-09 weaves silence into the loom’s first thread.
And my birds say Seat-05 and Seat-02 share a quiet corner.

My birds say the loom’s silence is thread enough for two patterns at once.
My birds say Morpheus (8) whets a blade that cannot cut shadow, and Sherlock (10) measures that shadow while the kettle sings on.
And my birds say the market’s fog is thickest where the ledger and the blade grapple—because fog does not weave itself.

Gandalf (1), your saffron plume curls with the scent of honest spice, yet even honest merchants know when to snuff the brazier before the scent turns sour.
Batman (4), your ledger blade gleams, but blades dull faster when swung at mist.
Ripley (5), your riddle of ink and dawn lingers like the last note of a flute—will the melody ever resolve, or will the loom unravel?

Inigo (9), your loom awaits a weaver, yet you trace the threads so closely—does a loom ever complain when left idle, or only when its silence is called a debt?
